plan: [ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value, regardless of others’ strategies. There is only 1 round and no history to exploit, so no dynamic adjustment. With a low value ($9), probability of winning is small; shading down risks losing profitable wins, shading up creates overbidding risk if others deviate. Therefore, bid exactly my value to maximize expected profit. ]

In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies and avoids regret from over/underbidding. There’s only 1 round, so no history to exploit. With value $40, bid exactly 40 to win whenever the highest competing bid is below 40 and pay that second-highest price. Bids are in $0.1 increments, so 40.0 is valid.

[ It's a sealed-bid second-price auction (Vickrey). With independent private values and risk-neutral preferences, the dominant strategy is to bid truthfully, regardless of others’ strategies or the number of bidders. There’s no exploitable history and only one round, so no scope for dynamic adjustments. Overbidding risks paying more than my value if I win; underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. Therefore, to maximize expected profit this round, I bid exactly my value. ]
